title: 2017 AMC 12A 17
statement: There are \(24\) different complex numbers \(z\) such that \(z^{24}=1.\) For how many of these is \(z^6\) a real number?

solutions.text:
The \(24\) solutions are the \(24\)th roots of unity, \(z=e^{\frac{\pi i k}{12}}\) for \(k=0,1,\ldots,23.\)

Then \(z^6=e^{\frac{\pi i k}{2}}=\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{k\pi}{2},\) which is real exactly when \(\sin\dfrac{k\pi}{2}=0,\) i.e. when \(k\) is even. There are \(12\) even values of \(k\) in the range.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Then \(z^6=e^{\frac{\pi i k}{2}},\) which is real exactly when \(k\) is even
